author: business-analyst
text: BL-0010 review: The story captures the supplied per-invocation, per-Activity separation and repeated-spawn intent. No unresolved product decision blocks refinement. Low-severity testability improvement: explicitly test simultaneous invocations and verify that the folder exists and its location is supplied when each invocation starts; retain earlier files. Proposed acceptance wording, not an agreed decision: Given two invocations in the same Activity, including concurrent invocations of the same agent, each receives a different existing folder under that Activity at invocation start; a file written in one remains intact and absent from the other. Given an invocation in another Activity, its folder is under that Activity. Folder naming and cleanup remain unspecified; do not infer a retention policy beyond the stated non-overwrite requirement. Review only; no implementation or backlog changes.

author: software-developer
text: BL-0010 implementation assessment: runtime host.py explicitly reports invocation unsupported; a runtime allocator alone cannot bind a folder to a real spawn. Add an Activity-owned, exclusive per-invocation allocation under the runtime lock after validating the stable current ID, and have the actual host allocate before each new spawn and pass that path in the assignment. Use a fresh opaque UUID per spawn attempt, never agent name alone; retain failed or uncertain attempts and allocate anew for a retry. A follow-up to an existing running agent should retain its original allocation, while a new spawn gets a new one. Serialize allocation with closure and prevent closure while assigned agents may still write; archive preserves the subtree via the existing Activity rename. Test concurrent allocations, repeated agent names, collision/no-overwrite, mismatched or closed Activities, partial allocation/spawn failure, and archive continuity. Host integration and its observable spawn identity are the principal implementation dependency; do not claim end-to-end coverage from allocator tests alone.

author: quality-assurance

BA's start-time wording is a proposal, not an approved change. Test exclusive creation/collision, path traversal and links, partial or failed launch and archive/active-path reuse races; define follow-up versus new invocation and retention/lifecycle behavior rather than assuming them. Existing runtime has cooperative locking and archive rename but does not spawn agents; isolated fixture tests cannot alone prove actual host handoff. No implementation tests were run.

author: solution-architect
text: BL-0010 architecture/planning review: recommend runtime-owned allocation under the current Activity before each new host spawn, with a fresh opaque invocation ID, exclusive directory creation, stable Activity attribution and an existing path supplied to the agent. No runtime host-spawn wrapper is available or proposed. Same-live-instance follow-up retaining its folder is a proposed boundary; repeated/new spawns always receive fresh folders. Allocation failures block launch; failed or uncertain launches retain allocations. Archive retains all supporting material, and host must finish relevant writers before closure because the runtime allocation lock does not stop agent file writes. Developer and QA recommendations were relayed by host and reconciled: real host handoff/use evidence is required in addition to runtime fixtures. Four-phase draft covers contract, allocator, host handoff and acceptance verification. Original story remains authority; BA refinement and lifecycle defaults remain proposals. No implementation or tests executed.
